held_new.title: Interrupted runs skip restoration
held_new.reason: The code-level claim is exact. mutants_core.main() runs the per-mutant cycle as three bare statements - POLICY.write_text(fn(orig)); p = _run_test(); POLICY.write_text(orig) - with no try/finally. If _run_test() raises (OSError launching the subprocess) or the operator interrupts mid-run, the third statement is skipped and runtime/mission-chaining.md is left holding the mutant. main() re-reads `orig = POLICY.read_text()` at entry, so a rerun in that same checkout would indeed adopt the mutant as its baseline. The suggested finally-block is the correct and cheap fix.
held_new.severity_assessment: Correctly rated P2 / non-blocking, and arguably even weaker than stated, because the stated consequence is NOT silent. The `fixed-head` positive control runs FIRST, against `orig`, before any mutant: on a corrupted baseline it goes non-GREEN and main() appends 'fixed-head control is not GREEN' and exits 1. For a leftover neutral (expected-GREEN) reflow the control would pass, but the later sub() patterns would then miss and those mutants would report as SURVIVORS - also exit 1. Either way the harness FAILS CLOSED rather than quietly measuring against the wrong policy. This is the fail-closed property r3 was dispatched to add, doing its job.
held_new.residual_risk: Operator-facing, not evidence-facing: a dirty checkout after an interrupt. The module docstring already directs the harness to be run 'in a DISPOSABLE checkout', and `git status` was clean after both of this round's runs.
held_new.scope: inside this unit's own evidence harness (docs/reports/U-CHAIN/), NOT the frozen spec (runtime/mission-chaining.md)
held_new.note_for_batch: Same scope class as BOT-5 and a direct descendant of it: BOT-5 attacked the harness's baseline SOURCE (an untracked fixture), BOT-6 attacks the harness's baseline INTEGRITY across an aborted run. The r3 fix hardened the source (baseline() derives from a pinned SHA and hash-checks it); it did not wrap the mutate/run cycle. HELD per dispatch - fix NOTHING.
